label: The distractor-state control kills the verdict: with each row's state rotated to the next row's, the recorded run prints verdict jev: kill K=40 M=40 A=0 B=30 W=0 L=30 F=0 p=0.0000 and W+L=30 interval95=[0.000,0.114]; all 30 discordant rows are losses where the model picked the folder named in the rotated state. The judgment is state-anchored, not content-anchored — a P0 robustness failure of the question shape.

The keep survives only with path-resolved descriptions and the original state: re-measure keep K=40 M=40 A=39 B=30 W=10 L=1 F=0 p=0.0059 baseline=top (311 calls, 102 s), recall 40/40, baseline target=0 top=30 comparator=auto. The ten wins are rows whose label is neither target nor top — real recoveries the distractor control then invalidates as a live predictor.

The corpus is a fixture by construction (target wrong 0/40; labels one arbiter read; comparator=auto chosen on the scored labels) and 11 discordant rows cannot prove a live win (80% power needs 69 at a 0.65 win rate). Proving needs real low-match saves with final destination and label provenance, a pre-declared comparator, a holdout, and either >=69 discordant pairs or an explicit screen-only acceptance.
sources: computed: sign-test power (iteration 3 script, same rule family)

label: f022-001 still loses with both options described: Jev picks 007-classifier-deep-research at 0.48, 0.58 and 0.43 against the label 001-deep-research. The path-resolved describer fix removed the undescribed-option defect but did not convert the one loss; the row should be adjudicated, not chased.

The trust upgrades landed: kill branch (kill P(X>=L)<=0.05), W+L Wilson interval, discordant rows, corpus/report/scorer pins, label-swap control (W+L=10 [0.722,1.000]; wins sit on rows whose label is neither target nor top), distractor-state arm, and a confidence-gated arm keeping the same verdict at 70 choice calls vs 120. Tests grew 35 to 43.

Integration shape: add 'alignment-suggestion' with env JEV_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT_SUGGESTION to FEATURES and an interactive, flag-gated save-flow suggestion that asks featureReady first, shows one folder with a reason, and lets the existing selection step authorize any switch; never override the below-20% hard block; CLI-explicit saves keep their folder; consent + timeout + kill switch; a 047 D6 amendment is required.

Tests to cover beyond the landed 43 cases: a masked-state variant test (state with folder names removed), a real-save corpus validation fixture with final destinations, label-provenance assertions, an f022-001 adjudication record, and interactive-flow integration tests with a stub jev (fail-open, timeout, consent). The masked-state ablation is the highest-value new test because it probes the distractor failure directly.

Ranked next step: build the same 40-row arm with folder names masked out of the state (or an explicit instruction to ignore state folder names) and rerun the distractor-state control; if the kill persists, retire the current question shape with that evidence; if it survives, the feature earns a real-save corpus. One arm run plus a small scorer change gates everything else.
